subject.title: fix(ollama): remote Ollama streaming stalls at model_call:started on slow hosts

question: Should native Ollama timeoutSeconds be accepted as an idle/no-progress timeout for streaming responses, and what proof is required before merge?
rationale: The code shape matches sibling streaming wrappers, but current Ollama docs and current behavior describe timeoutSeconds as a total guarded-fetch cap, so automation cannot decide the compatibility tradeoff without maintainer intent.

options.title: Require proof and document idle semantics
options.body: Ask for redacted remote or slow Ollama OpenClaw output and align the Ollama timeout documentation before merge.

options.title: Accept sibling parity without doc changes
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally accept the idle-timeout behavior based on the shared guarded-body contract, but users may still see a documentation mismatch.

options.title: Keep total timeout semantics
options.body: Reject this approach and require a different fix that preserves timeoutSeconds as a wall-clock cap for native Ollama streams.

recommendation.title: Require proof and document idle semantics
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted remote or slow Ollama OpenClaw output and align the Ollama timeout documentation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to steipete as the broadest provider/network runtime owner for deciding timeout compatibility semantics.
